answer: To make Sybil identities costly, require every worker to lock a refundable bond before entering a trellis of independently assigned tasks; release it only after auditors verify distinct outputs. A farm creating 1,000 accounts must immobilize 1,000 bonds for the review period, paying the same capital and opportunity cost per identity, while duplicate work is slashed. Random task routing makes each fake account wander across reviewers instead of sharing one easy gate, and rewards follow verified useful work, not account count—a voyage of accounts earns nothing if their outputs fail.
